summary:
MARSIGHT is a planetary terrain exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map." It connects Mars terrain dataset discovery with scientific raster analysis, helping users explore and interpret planetary elevation information.

Using a real HiRISE Digital Terrain Model (DTM), MARSIGHT provides dataset metadata, elevation statistics, bounded raster-window processing and elevation profile sampling through a web-based interface and scientific API. Its processing workflow accounts for NoData pixels and preserves dataset provenance, supporting more transparent and reproducible terrain analysis.

Built with Python, FastAPI, Rasterio, NumPy, React, TypeScript and Cesium, MARSIGHT aims to make complex planetary terrain data more accessible. Its modular architecture provides a foundation for expanding to additional datasets and future terrain-analysis capabilities, supporting research and future planetary exploration workflows.
details:
What MARSIGHT Does

  • Provides a web-based platform for discovering and exploring Martian terrain datasets.
  • Uses a selected HiRISE Digital Terrain Model (DTM).
  • Retrieves scientific metadata and elevation statistics.
  • Supports bounded raster-window processing and elevation profile sampling.
  • Handles NoData pixels to avoid treating invalid measurements as real terrain.
  • Preserves dataset identification and scientific provenance.

How It Works

  1. Discover the selected planetary terrain dataset.
  2. Inspect its metadata and scientific reference information.
  3. Configure the raster source through the backend dataset registry.
  4. Process raster information using Python, Rasterio and NumPy.
  5. Expose processing results through a FastAPI scientific API.
  6. Present available information through a React and Cesium-based web interface.

Impact and Benefits

  • Makes complex planetary terrain information easier to access and interpret.
  • Connects dataset discovery with scientific raster processing.
  • Encourages transparent and reproducible planetary data analysis.
  • Provides a foundation for future planetary research and exploration tools.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite and Cesium.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Scientific processing: Rasterio and NumPy.
  • Data: NASA/HiRISE Mars Digital Terrain Model.

Creativity and Innovation

  • Combines planetary dataset discovery, scientific metadata and raster processing in one platform.
  • Uses a configurable dataset registry and bounded processing operations.
  • Separates the user interface, API and scientific processing layers.
  • Emphasises scientific provenance and explicit handling of invalid raster pixels.

Feasibility and Scalability

  • Built using established open-source geospatial and web technologies.
  • Modular architecture supports the addition of more planetary terrain datasets.
  • Bounded raster operations provide a foundation for working with larger datasets.
  • Future enhancements may include validated terrain visualisation, additional terrain products, scalable storage and terrain-aware exploration planning.

Scientific Transparency

  • The selected HiRISE DTM contains 11,364,103 pixels.
  • 9,537,521 valid pixels and 1,826,582 NoData pixels.
  • Verified reference elevation range: 2908.53 m to 3259.00 m.
  • Reported automated validation: 35 backend tests and 7 frontend tests passed.
  • Actual raster statistics are distinguished from mock visual elements and planned features.
  • Terrain-aware routing and real raster surface rendering are not claimed as implemented capabilities.
